name: @javakha77/mcp

tools.name: deposit
tools.description: Shields your own funds: wallet public balance -> its private (shielded) balance. Use when the user says deposit/shield. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. No Hinkal fee, only gas. For someone else's private balance use deposit_for_other.

tokenAddress.description: Token SYMBOL (e.g. "USDC", "ETH") or on-chain address (EVM 0x, Solana mint, Tron T.../0x). Pass the symbol directly for common tokens; only call list_tokens if a symbol fails to resolve.

amount.description: Token amount in human decimal units (e.g. "1.5" tokens), NOT wei/base units

tools.name: withdraw
tools.description: Unshields funds: private (shielded) balance -> any public address. Use when the user says withdraw/unshield/cash out. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. Fee is on top: the private balance must cover amount + fee.

tokenAddress.description: Token SYMBOL (e.g. "USDC", "ETH") or on-chain address (EVM 0x, Solana mint, Tron T.../0x). Pass the symbol directly for common tokens; only call list_tokens if a symbol fails to resolve.

amount.description: Token amount in human decimal units (e.g. "1.5" tokens), NOT wei/base units

toAddress.description: Public address that receives the tokens

tools.name: deposit_for_other
tools.description: Your wallet public balance -> ANOTHER user's private (shielded) balance. Use to gift or fund someone privately. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. No Hinkal fee, only gas. Recipient must be the public address of a registered Hinkal wallet. For your own balance use deposit.

tokenAddress.description: Token SYMBOL (e.g. "USDC", "ETH") or on-chain address (EVM 0x, Solana mint, Tron T.../0x). Pass the symbol directly for common tokens; only call list_tokens if a symbol fails to resolve.

amount.description: Token amount in human decimal units (e.g. "1.5" tokens), NOT wei/base units

recipient.description: Recipient's public address; must belong to a registered Hinkal wallet so its private address can be resolved

tools.name: private_transfer
tools.description: Your private (shielded) balance -> another Hinkal user's private balance, with no public trace of sender, recipient, or amount. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. Fee is on top: the balance must cover amount + fee. Recipient must be the public address of a registered Hinkal wallet; for an arbitrary address use private_send or withdraw.

tokenAddress.description: Token SYMBOL (e.g. "USDC", "ETH") or on-chain address (EVM 0x, Solana mint, Tron T.../0x). Pass the symbol directly for common tokens; only call list_tokens if a symbol fails to resolve.

amount.description: Token amount in human decimal units (e.g. "1.5" tokens), NOT wei/base units

recipient.description: Public address of a registered Hinkal wallet; the transfer lands in its private (shielded) balance

tools.name: recover_stuck_funds
tools.description: Withdraws stuck UTXOs of one token to a public address. Use only after get_stuck_balances reports stuck funds. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. Returns one transaction hash per recovered UTXO batch.

tokenAddress.description: Token SYMBOL (e.g. "USDC", "ETH") or on-chain address (EVM 0x, Solana mint, Tron T.../0x). Pass the symbol directly for common tokens; only call list_tokens if a symbol fails to resolve.

toAddress.description: Public address that receives the recovered tokens

tools.name: private_send
tools.description: Unlinkable payout: your wallet public balance -> one or more public addresses, with no on-chain link between sender and recipients. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. One transaction per recipient, each returning a txHash and a scheduleId; payouts complete asynchronously - poll check_private_send_status per scheduleId. Recipients receive the full amount; the fee is charged on top.

tokenAddress.description: Token SYMBOL (e.g. "USDC", "ETH") or on-chain address (EVM 0x, Solana mint, Tron T.../0x). Pass the symbol directly for common tokens; only call list_tokens if a symbol fails to resolve.

address.description: Public address that receives the tokens

amount.description: Token amount in human decimal units (e.g. "1.5" tokens), NOT wei/base units

recipients.description: One or more recipients, each with a public address and an amount in human decimal units

tools.name: wallet_sign_message
tools.description: Signs an arbitrary message with your wallet for the given chain and returns the signature (personal_sign style on EVM/Tron, base64 ed25519 on Solana). Nothing is broadcast, but the signature is an authorization someone can redeem later. Show the user what is being signed and confirm before signing anything that grants a token allowance or trade.

message.description: Message to sign; signed as UTF-8 text

tools.name: wallet_sign_typed_data
tools.description: Signs EIP-712 typed data (domain, types, value) with your wallet and returns the signature. EVM chains only. A Permit or order payload lets whoever holds it move funds later. Nothing is broadcast, but the signature is an authorization someone can redeem later. Show the user what is being signed and confirm before signing anything that grants a token allowance or trade.

domain.description: EIP-712 domain object (name, version, chainId, verifyingContract, ...)

types.description: EIP-712 types object mapping struct names to their field definitions

value.description: EIP-712 message value object to sign

tools.name: wallet_send
tools.description: Plain PUBLIC on-chain transfer of native or ERC-20/TRC-20/SPL tokens from your wallet - fully visible on-chain, NO privacy. For a private payout use private_send or withdraw. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous.

tokenAddress.description: Token SYMBOL (e.g. "USDC", "ETH") or on-chain address (EVM 0x, Solana mint, Tron T.../0x). Pass the symbol directly for common tokens; only call list_tokens if a symbol fails to resolve.

amount.description: Token amount in human decimal units (e.g. "1.5" tokens), NOT wei/base units

toAddress.description: Public address that receives the tokens

tools.name: wallet_approve
tools.description: Sets an ERC-20/TRC-20 allowance from your wallet to a spender contract. EVM and Tron only. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous.

tokenAddress.description: Token SYMBOL (e.g. "USDC", "ETH") or on-chain address (EVM 0x, Solana mint, Tron T.../0x). Pass the symbol directly for common tokens; only call list_tokens if a symbol fails to resolve.

spender.description: Contract or address receiving the allowance

amount.description: Token amount in human decimal units (e.g. "1.5" tokens), NOT wei/base units

tools.name: wallet_execute
tools.description: Arbitrary contract call from your wallet: on EVM pass calldata in data (plus optional value); on Tron pass functionSelector and parameters. Not for Solana - use wallet_solana_execute. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous.

data.description: EVM calldata (0x-prefixed hex). Required on EVM chains, ignored on Tron

value.description: Optional native value to attach, in human decimal units

functionSelector.description: Tron function selector, e.g. "transfer(address,uint256)". Required on Tron, ignored on EVM

parameters.description: Tron call parameters matching the functionSelector. Required on Tron, ignored on EVM

tools.name: wallet_solana_execute
tools.description: Signs and broadcasts a base64 serialized Solana VersionedTransaction with your wallet. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous.

transaction.description: Base64 serialized Solana VersionedTransaction to sign and broadcast

tools.name: tron_freeze
tools.description: Freezes TRX from your wallet to obtain ENERGY or BANDWIDTH on Tron. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous.

amount.description: TRX amount in human decimal units

tools.name: tron_unfreeze
tools.description: Unfreezes previously frozen TRX (ENERGY or BANDWIDTH) on Tron. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous.

amount.description: TRX amount in human decimal units

tools.name: tron_delegate_resource
tools.description: Delegates frozen ENERGY or BANDWIDTH from your wallet to another Tron address. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous.

toAddress.description: Public address that receives the tokens

amount.description: TRX amount in human decimal units

tools.name: get_all_balances
tools.description: Use when the user asks for their balances or portfolio without naming a single chain. Fetches public AND private (shielded) balances of your wallet on every supported chain in ONE call, grouped per chain; only non-zero tokens appear. For a single chain use get_balances or get_public_balances.

tools.name: get_balances
tools.description: Use when the user asks about their private/shielded Hinkal balance on ONE chain, per token, in human and base units; only non-zero appear. Public wallet balances are separate (get_public_balances); for every chain at once use get_all_balances.

refresh.description: Set true if balances look stale (e.g. right after a deposit was broadcast) to re-scan before reading

tools.name: get_stuck_balances
tools.description: Use when the user asks about stuck funds/utxos. Returns blocked UTXOs left by a private_send whose withdraw leg never completed - all chains, per token, grouped per wallet address (EVM, Tron, Solana). Separate from the spendable balance in get_balances. Recover with recover_stuck_funds.

tools.name: get_public_balances
tools.description: Use when the user asks about their public/on-chain wallet balance on ONE chain, per token, in human and base units; only non-zero appear. Does NOT check gas. Defaults to your wallet; pass walletAddress to check any other address. For every chain at once use get_all_balances.

walletAddress.description: Wallet to check; defaults to your Hinkal wallet

tools.name: list_chains
tools.description: Rarely needed - chain ids are standard (1 = Ethereum, 137 = Polygon, etc.); use only to discover an unknown chain. Lists every supported chain with numeric chainId, name, and type (evm = 0x, solana = base58, tron = T... addresses). No account required.

tools.name: list_tokens
tools.description: Rarely needed - transaction tools accept a token symbol (e.g. "USDC") directly, so use only when a symbol fails to resolve or the user wants to browse tokens. Lists common tokens for the chain; optional case-insensitive symbol/name filter. No account required.

search.description: Optional case-insensitive filter on token symbol or name

tools.name: get_wallet_status
tools.description: Wallet state: none (set up automatically on the first tool call that needs it) or active, with the wallet addresses when available. No wallet setup required.

tools.name: check_private_send_status
tools.description: Checks the status of a private send payout by scheduleId (returned by private_send, one per recipient). Returns the scheduled payout transactions. Requires the account that created the send - others get a not-found error.

scheduleId.description: scheduleId returned by private_send for a recipient

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Checks the Hinkal API is up. Use it to distinguish a real outage from a bad-request error when another tool fails. No account required.

tools.name: get_contract_addresses
tools.description: Deployed Hinkal contract addresses per chain id (hinkalAddress, plus hinkalHelperAddress, hinkalWrapperAddress, depositOnChainUtxosExternalActionAddress where applicable). Tells you which contract a token allowance must be granted to before deposit. EVM chains only. No account required.

tools.name: get_enclave_public_key
tools.description: Current public key of the Hinkal enclave, used to encrypt payloads to it. Pair with get_enclave_attestation, which reports the verificationPublicKey the attestation vouches for. No account required.

tools.name: get_enclave_attestation
tools.description: Use when the user wants to verify the enclave. Returns the attestation proving the Hinkal API runs in a genuine secure enclave: jwt (signed, covers your nonce), imageDigest (running image), verificationPublicKey (key it vouches for). In local crypto mode only verificationPublicKey is returned (no jwt/imageDigest) - nothing is attested then, so never treat it as proof. No account required.

nonce.description: Caller-generated nonce echoed inside the attestation document, proving it was produced for this request rather than replayed. Use a fresh random value each time.

tools.name: get_wallet_addresses
tools.description: Returns the public EVM, Tron, and Solana addresses of your Hinkal wallet. This is the address to FUND before a deposit (token + native gas).

tools.name: export_wallet_key
tools.description: Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks to export or back up the wallet. SENSITIVE: reveals the private access key (full wallet control) plus restore instructions; it appears in this conversation, so warn the user and get explicit confirmation before calling it. Never call it on your own initiative.

instructions:
WALLET ON THIS SERVER:
- Set up AUTOMATICALLY on first use and kept across restarts. Never ask the user for a wallet address or chain to "connect" - just call the tool you need.
- Every transaction is signed and broadcast SERVER-SIDE by Hinkal; there is nothing for you to sign.
- The wallet starts EMPTY. Before the first deposit, call get_wallet_addresses and tell the user to fund the address for their chain (token + native gas).

Hinkal moves tokens between the wallet's PUBLIC balance and its PRIVATE (shielded) Hinkal balance on each supported chain. Amounts are human decimal units (e.g. "1.5"), never wei.

Keep to the fewest steps: confirm token, amount, chain, and recipient, then call the one tool with the token SYMBOL (e.g. "USDC"), amount, and chainId. Chain ids are standard (1 = Ethereum, 137 = Polygon). Do NOT preflight with list_tokens, list_chains, get_balances, or get_public_balances - tools accept symbols, and a spend self-reports any missing balance, gas, or allowance. Use those lookups only when a call fails or the user asks for balances.

Choosing the fund-moving tool (each runs server-side and returns a txHash):
- shield own funds -> deposit; fund someone ELSE privately -> deposit_for_other
- pay from shielded balance, fully private -> private_transfer (recipient must be a registered Hinkal wallet)
- unlinkable payout to any public address(es) -> private_send
- unshield to a public address -> withdraw
- wallet_send and other wallet_* tools are plain PUBLIC actions, no privacy - only when the user asks.

Reporting a result: show the FULL txHash and any scheduleId (never truncate), and render an explorerUrl as a markdown [View on explorer](url) on its own line. After a spend, report the txHash and expected balance directly - do not call get_balances to verify unless asked (it re-scans and is slow).
